messages:
Samir: Quick proposal: per-key quotas should be split by endpoint type. chat = token-rate + qps, embeddings = rps + compute-cost weight, rerank = rps, streaming = concurrent connections.
Maya: +1. Also need an org-level shared burst pool so customers don't blow all quota on embeddings spike and kill chat latency.
Jon: Implementation note: token-rate vs request-rate means we must measure tokens at the ingress layer. Any perf hit?
Maya: We can sample for costs, but exact token counts already flow through the runtime for billing. reuse that metric.
Nina: For streaming, concurrent-count is the right knob. We should avoid token-based for streams because it's open-ended.
Pat: UX question: how do we show this in Console? Per-endpoint rows with current usage + projected throttling window.
Samir: Dashboard: per-endpoint SLOs, token burn rate, predicted time-to-throttle. Add a 'burst remaining' metric.
OpsBot: deploy:rate-limits v2 scheduled to canary @staging at 12:15 UTC
Maya: Edge case: retries from clients can amplify bursts. We need leaky-bucket + retry-aware headers (Retry-After) and quota-alarm.
Jon: Internal API debate: enforce at gateway vs at runtime. Gateway cheaper but lacks token visibility; runtime accurate but adds latency.
Nina: I'd prefer hybrid: gate basic rps/carveouts at gateway, exact token enforcement at runtime with fallback tokens if gateway denies.
Samir: Example config draft:
```
rate_limits:
  scope: api_key
  endpoints:
    chat: {qps: 20, burst: 60, token_rate_per_sec: 300}
    embeddings: {rps: 8, burst: 30, cost_weight: 3}
    rerank: {rps: 12, burst: 25}
    streaming: {concurrent: 5}
  org_shared_burst: 200
```
Pat: We should run a sim against past 30 days traffic to see throttle impact. Nina can you run sim by EOD?
Nina: On it. will post results in this thread.
Samir: Cool. next steps: Nina runs sim, Jon prototypes gateway hook, Maya updates console mockups. Ping me if blocked. :thumbsup:
